items.title: Where Each Grade of Practice Leads to Be Reborn

items.zh: 復次，此中於初靜慮下中上品善修習已，隨其所應，當生梵眾天、梵輔天、大梵天眾同分中。於第二靜慮下中上品善修習已，隨其所應，當生少光天、無量光天、極光淨天眾同分中。於第三靜慮下中上品善修習已，隨其所應，當生少淨天、無量淨天、遍淨天眾同分中。於第四靜慮下中上品善修習已，隨其所應，當生無雲天、福生天、廣果天眾同分中。
items.en: Furthermore, in this regard, having well cultivated the first dhyāna to a lower, middle, or upper grade, one will, as appropriate, be reborn among the retinue of the heaven of Brahmā's Multitude, the heaven of Brahmā's Ministers, or the Great Brahmā heaven … having well cultivated the fourth dhyāna to a lower, middle, or upper grade, one will, as appropriate, be reborn among the retinue of the Cloudless heaven, the heaven of Born of Merit, or the heaven of Vast Reward.

items.zh: 若不還者，以無漏第四靜慮間雜熏修有漏第四靜慮；即於此中，下品、中品、上品、上勝品、上極品善修習已，隨其所應，當生五淨居天眾同分中。謂無煩、無熱、善現、善見、色究竟天。
items.en: If a non-returner, interspersing the fourth dhyāna's uncontaminated form with cultivation of its contaminated form, well cultivates this to a lower, middle, upper, superior-upper, or utmost-upper grade, one will, as appropriate, be reborn among the retinue of the five pure-abode heavens — namely, the heavens of No Affliction, No Heat, Sublime Appearance, Sublime Vision, and the Peak of Form.

items.zh: 若於空處、識處、無所有處、非想非非想處，下中上品善修習已，當生空處、識處、無所有處、非想非非想處隨行天眾同分中。由彼諸天無有形色，是故亦無處所差別。
items.en: If one has well cultivated the sphere of space, of consciousness, of nothingness, or of neither-perception-nor-non-perception to a lower, middle, or upper grade, one will be reborn among the heavenly beings of the sphere of space, of consciousness, of nothingness, or of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, who are reborn there solely by following their karmic practice. Since those heavenly beings have no physical form at all, there is likewise no difference of location among them.

items.zh: 然住所作有其差別。於無想定善修習已，當生無想有情天眾同分中。復次，此中云何應知離欲者相？

items.title: Section: The Marks of One Freed from Desire — Body, Speech, and Mind

items.zh: 謂離欲者，身業安住，諸根無動，威儀進止無有躁擾，於一威儀能經時久，不多驚懼，終不數數易脫威儀。言詞柔軟、言詞寂靜，不樂諠雜、不樂眾集，言語安詳。
items.en: One who is free of desire has bodily conduct that is settled, faculties that are unmoving, comportment free of any agitation, able to remain in a single posture for a long stretch of time, not easily startled or frightened, and never repeatedly shifting out of whatever posture is held. Their speech is gentle, their speech is calm; they take no delight in noise and clamour, no delight in crowds and gatherings; their manner of speaking is composed.

items.zh: 眼見色已，唯覺了色，不因覺了而起色貪；如是耳聞聲已、鼻嗅香已、舌甞味已、身覺觸已，唯覺了聲乃至其觸，不因覺了而起聲貪乃至觸貪。能無所畏，覺慧幽深，輕安廣大，身心隱密，無有貪婪、無有憤發，能有堪忍，不為種種欲尋思等諸惡尋思擾亂其心。
items.en: Having seen a form with the eye, one merely apprehends the form, without giving rise, on account of that apprehension, to craving for form; likewise, having heard a sound, smelled a scent, tasted a flavour, or felt a touch, one merely apprehends the sound and so on up through the touch, without craving arising on their account. One is able to be without any fear, one's discernment runs deep and quiet, one's pliancy is vast, body and mind are securely sealed against disturbance, without greed, without eruption of anger, able to endure whatever comes, and the mind is not disturbed by thoughts of desire or any other unwholesome thought.

items.zh: 如是等類，當知名為離欲者相。

blocks.text: A short day to close fascicle 33: the heavens each level of absorption leads to, and how a person free of desire appears.

The first absorption, practised to a lower, middle, or upper grade, leads to rebirth among Brahmā's retinue, Brahmā's ministers, or the Great Brahmā heaven. The second, third, and fourth likewise lead to their three heavens each.
"A non-returner, interspersing the fourth absorption's uncontaminated form with its contaminated form", practised to five grades, is reborn in the five pure abodes.
The formless attainments lead to rebirth in the corresponding formless spheres. Master Cháng Bǎi: since these beings have no form, there is no difference of place among them.

subs.head: Marks of one free of desire

blocks.text: "Bodily conduct settled, faculties unmoving, comportment free of agitation; able to remain in a single posture for a long time; not easily startled." "Having seen a form with the eye, one merely apprehends the form, without craving for it"; likewise for sounds, smells, tastes, touches. "Their speech is gentle and calm; they take no delight in noise and crowds." "Body and mind are securely sealed against disturbance; able to endure whatever comes."

The mundane path, in full: seven attentions, four absorptions, four formless spheres, two mindless attainments, and the supernormal powers. Fascicle 34, the last of the Śrāvaka Stage, turns to the supramundane path: the direct realisation of the four truths.

quiz.q: Formless heavens "have no form, so no difference of location." Why "dwelling accordingly," according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: no intermediate state and no difference of environment
quiz.why: "Since those heavenly beings have no physical form at all, there is likewise no difference of location among them." Venerable Miào Jìng: they have no intermediate body, nor any difference of environment — hence "dwelling accordingly."

quiz.q: The detached "remain long in one posture, never shifting." What examples do the masters give?
options: Miào Jìng: lying down and never moving shows practice — not only sitting; Cháng Bǎi: a monk lay till dawn without moving — quilt and pillow untouched
quiz.why: "Able to remain in a single posture for a long stretch of time, not easily startled, and never repeatedly shifting out of whatever posture is held." Venerable Miào Jìng: lying there without ever moving — that shows practice; it's not that only sitting shows practice. Master Cháng Bǎi: he lay down and didn't move until dawn — quilt and pillow undisturbed.
